_comment: Every third party that installs or updates HelixScreen with its own tooling, and what it
pulls from a release. scripts/distribution_partners.py reads this file twice: release.yml
fails a release that is missing an asset listed here, and the table in
docs/devel/INSTALLER.md § Distribution Partners is rendered from it (`table --write`).
fetches[].asset is an exact release asset name; {tag} stands for the release tag (v1.2.3).
fetches[].built_by is the release.yml build matrix platform that produces the asset, or
`installer` for install.sh, so a dry run that builds a platform subset requires only what
it built. fetches[].via says whose code names the asset: `partner` when the mod's own code
hardcodes it, `installer` when the mod runs our install.sh and the name is the one
install.sh asks for on that hardware.
sources cite where each cell comes from, with the commit read. Contacts and owners are
Preston's call and stay TBD until he sets them.

partners.name: Z-Mod
partners.hardware: AD5M / AD5M Pro, AD5X, Creator 5 Pro
partners.finds_release: Moonraker `type: web` update manager on repo `prestonbrown/helixscreen` (GitHub latest release), downloading the asset named by the `asset_name` that Z-Mod seeds in /srv/helixscreen/release_info.json
partners.install_source: none: Z-Mod extracts the zip itself and never runs install.sh
partners.starts: Z-Mod's own `S80helixscreen` from `/srv/helixscreen`, selected with `DISPLAY_OFF HELIX=1`
partners.incumbent_screen: Stock screen; GuppyScreen and HelixScreen are both offered
sources: https://github.com/ghzserg/z_ad5x/blob/b3931ad80ec42496f948c9b780bb5216ec68ca1c/.shell/root/start.sh (release_info.json seeding; same lines in z_ff5m 5634a8b8f9 and z_c5pro 6d5a8709c1)

partners.name: Forge-X
partners.finds_release: Forge-X has no HelixScreen code. The user runs our install.sh, which reads the R2 channel manifest and falls back to the GitHub release; on a Forge-X host it installs the payload contract
partners.starts: The service lands in the mod chroot's `/etc/init.d`, started by Forge-X's own bootstrap (INSTALLER.md § Mod-Managed Hosts)
sources: scripts/lib/installer/release.sh#_release_candidates (zip by fixed name, tar by tag)

partners.name: PAXX (Snapmaker U1 Extended Firmware)
partners.finds_release: `extended-pkg helixscreen download` fetches `https://github.com/prestonbrown/helixscreen/releases/download/v${PKG_VERSION}/<asset>` at the version pinned in the firmware, checked against a pinned sha256
partners.install_source: none: extended-pkg unpacks the archive and never runs install.sh
partners.starts: The lmd.d/30-helixscreen.sh hook bind-mounts `helix-screen` over `/usr/bin/gui` when `[components] gui` is `helixscreen`; in-app self-update is off
partners.incumbent_screen: Stock Snapmaker GUI; HelixScreen is an opt-in setting (Touchscreen GUI, Experimental)

partners.name: KIAUH
partners.hardware: Any Klipper host KIAUH manages (Pi, x86)
partners.finds_release: Our KIAUH extension pipes `https://releases.helixscreen.org/install.sh` into `sh`; install.sh then resolves the host's platform archive. Upstream KIAUH has no HelixScreen code; our installer copies the extension in
partners.incumbent_screen: None (a host tool; it also offers KlipperScreen)

partners.name: OpenCentauri COSmos
partners.finds_release: The firmware's Yocto recipe builds HelixScreen from source (`gitsm://` on `main` at a pinned SRCREV), so it fetches no release asset. Our install guide has users run install.sh, which fetches the cc1 archive
partners.starts: install.sh registers HelixScreen with COSmos's `gui-switcher` through an allowlist wrapper
partners.incumbent_screen: grumpyscreen, atomscreen or guppyscreen, chosen with `config-manager ui screen_ui`

partners.name: Creality Helper Script
partners.finds_release: Nothing: the script has no HelixScreen code. install.sh reserves `--source helper-script`, but nothing passes it yet

partners.name: Simple AF
partners.finds_release: Nothing: its installer only skips installing GrumpyScreen when `/etc/init.d/S99helixscreen` exists
